Twenty-three comments

Speed the plough

Source: Paul McGrattan (album: “The Frost is All Over”)
Transcription: Gian Marco Pietrasanta

↳ Posted by gian marco on August 18th, 2002.

The name Speed the Plough has a few tunes to its credit. One is a tune popular in Scotland with Country Dance bands and in England with Morris dancers. Another is an Irish tune, related to the Anglo-Scottish one, also known by a few other names, including Croghan Hill. The tune posted here, however, appears to be completely unrelated to either of the other two. I wonder how many of the recordings listed actually feature this tune.

Gannon, Smith, Blake

Colm Gannon, Jesse Smith and John Blake play a version of this tune under the name “McGreevy’s” as the opening tune on their album “The Ewe With The Crooked Horn”. They got it from a tape of Johnny McGreevy from Chicago playing at a late night party…

↳ Posted by wicklowpat on January 28th, 2015.

https://thesession.org/tunes/1191

Thanks for that article, Jeremy. Incidentally I ID’d about every title in the Henebry-O‘Neill Wax Cylinder Collection, which is what the author said he’d been up to - I put the titles in the comments on the Soundcloud files too. I think there’s only a couple of puzzlers out of the whole batch, almost all of it was commonplace enough. That article is about the other Speed the Plough: https://thesession.org/tunes/1191 That’s the tune I always use the STP title with, the one on this page I call O’Keefe’s Plough, that was Seamus Ennis’s title for it, the O’Keefe in question was famed Kerry fiddler Padraig O’K. Played a few tunes with some contra people last week and they had yet another tune going by this title, no idea about what it was though.

Speed The Plough, X:16

I first heard this tune being played by Johnny McCarthy, (button accordion), the late Michael Fitzgerald, (fiddle) and the late Sonny Murray, (concertina).

It seems to be a uniquely Ennis way of playing the tune, and I have not heard this version anywhere other than in Ennis.

There is a lovely little twist to the first part, and I have written out the full sixteen bars.

↳ Posted by John G McMahon on August 15th, 2025.
